summary: Microsoft retires two tiers of Azure Cache for Redis on March 31, 2027: Enterprise and Enterprise Flash. From April 1, 2027 every remaining Enterprise cache and every remaining Enterprise Flash cache is disabled. Creating new Enterprise or Enterprise Flash caches has been blocked since April 1, 2026. Reservations for both tiers are supported until March 30, 2027. Microsoft's replacement is Azure Managed Redis. Applications must switch to the new cache's hostname and access credentials. Azure Managed Redis is clustered by default, so applications should check that their client library works with a clustered cache. Basic, Standard and Premium caches retire later, in September 2028.
what_ends: Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise and Enterprise Flash tiers
previous_state: Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise and Enterprise Flash caches run normally until the retirement date.

summary: Microsoft retires the Basic, Standard and Premium tiers of Azure Cache for Redis on September 30, 2028. From October 1, 2028 every remaining Basic, Standard or Premium cache is disabled. Since April 1, 2026 new customers in Azure's public cloud cannot create caches in these tiers. A tenant that had any Azure Cache for Redis instance before April 1, 2026 can keep creating them until the retirement. Reservations are supported until September 30, 2028. Microsoft's replacement is Azure Managed Redis. Applications must switch to the new cache's hostname and access key. Azure Managed Redis is clustered by default, so the client library must be set up for a clustered cache.
what_ends: Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard and Premium tiers
previous_state: Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard and Premium caches run normally, and existing customers can still create them.
current_state: Microsoft Learn's "Azure Cache for Redis retirement FAQ" (last updated 2026-08-18, read 2026-11-15): "All instances of Azure Cache for Redis tiers (Basic, Standard, and Premium) will be retired on September 30, 2028." "Azure Managed Redis instances are clustered by default, so your application must configure your client library to work with a clustered Redis instance."
